recipe.title: Spicy Thai Basil Fried Rice (Khao Pad Kra Pao)
recipe.description: Fiery Thai street-food fried rice with holy basil, chilies, and a crispy fried egg. The rice absorbs the savory-sweet oyster sauce while the basil adds a peppery, aromatic finish. Day-old rice and screaming-hot wok heat are the secrets to the elusive wok hei char.

ingredients.name: Thai holy basil leaves
ingredients.notes: packed; sub Italian basil if unavailable — NOT Thai basil

ingredients.name: shallot
ingredients.notes: small, thinly sliced; optional but traditional in fried rice version

ingredients.name: prik nam pla
ingredients.notes: fish sauce with sliced chilies and lime — condiment, optional

steps.instruction: Pound the bird's eye chilies in a mortar to a fine paste. Add garlic and pound to a rough, broken paste — you want texture, not a smooth puree.
Combine oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. This is your seasoning sauce.

Heat a wok over highest heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil, then add the ground pork and spread into a thin layer. Let sear undisturbed for 45 seconds, then stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining 2 tbsp oil to the wok. Add the chili-garlic paste and shallot (if using). Stir-fry 30-45 seconds until very fragrant but not burnt.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with your spatula. Spread rice across the wok surface, let it sit 15-20 seconds to develop char, then toss. Repeat 2-3 times.
Pour the seasoning sauce over the rice and toss vigorously until every grain is evenly coated and rice is sizzling.
Return the cooked pork to the wok. Toss to combine and heat through.
Kill the heat. Add holy basil leaves and fold gently until they just wilt — residual heat is enough.
In a separate pan, fry eggs in oil over medium-high heat, spooning hot oil over the whites until the edges are crispy-lacy but yolk stays runny.
Plate rice, top with fried egg. Serve immediately with prik nam pla on the side.

recipe.sourceNotes: Adapted from Hot Thai Kitchen (Pailin Chongchitnant) — pad kra pao technique applied to fried rice method.
